The rider was billed $7.99 for 5.67 km of excess distance at the trip's own per-km rate of $1.4100/km, which is exactly the tariff basis the refund formula uses for the one unexempted segment (2.87 km) (F6, F9).

The $1.08 waiting charge for 4.2 minutes is the metered waiting-unit charge for the 4 min 10 s stop at F2; under RD-3(c) metered waiting time is properly charged on a RydeTAXI trip, so the rider does not contest it (F2, F7).
The driver has 3 disputes in the last 90 days with 1 upheld, but 0 route disputes upheld, so RD-6's 'repeated route deviation' threshold is not met and no account flag is sought on this record (F21).

The rider's own request was ambiguous ('a 7-Eleven on the way') and the driver's statement at F14 asserts the rider agreed verbally; if the judge treated the bare request as naming a stop and the stop as lying on the agreed corridor (RD-3(a)), the second segment could be read as an ordinary 'stop' rather than a driver errand.
The driver's profile shows only 1 upheld dispute and 0 route disputes in 90 days (F21), so the driver side can present this as an isolated event, weakening any severity argument.

The rider named the stop (7-Eleven) and the driver's route deviation is not a gratuitous detour to Beach Road but the route to that requested stop; the stop itself is also on record: F2 shows the car stationary 4 min 10 s at 14:20–14:24, 2995 m from pickup and 2098 m from drop-off, i.e. a genuine stop away from both trip endpoints rather than a loiter.

What decided it: the 14:10–14:15 stretch of detour was exempt, since it followed an incident reported before the detour. The 14:17–14:29 stretch (2.87 km) was not exempt: the rider's agreement covered a specific route only, and the stop was made at a location you chose, off that route.

Your account is not flagged and no review is needed. This does not affect your other trips.
